Sharp Vermont cheddar sauce grilled on toast.How to make it30g butter2 tbsp plain flour150ml milk1 tsp Dijon mustard1 tsp hot English mustard200g vintage cheddar, grated1 egg yolk4 thick slices of sourdough1 pinch cayenne pepperMelt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk until thick.Take off the heat and stir in both mustards, the cheese and yolk until smooth.Toast the bread on one side, spread the cheese mix thickly on the other and grill until bubbling and spotted brown.Dust with cayenne and serve hot.Food for worms pea and ham soupWe are food for worms lads. Split peas slow-cooked with a smoky hock.How to make it1 smoked ham hock500g green split peas, rinsed1 brown onion, diced2 carrots, diced2 celery sticks, diced2 bay leaves2 L water1 crusty loafPut the hock, peas, vegetables, bay leaves and water in a big pot and bring to the boil.Simmer gently, stirring now and then, until the peas collapse and the meat falls off the bone.Lift out the hock, shred the meat and stir it back in, then season.Serve with thick slices of the loaf.Main trayOpening night roast chicken with bread sauceNeil plays Puck at Henley Hall. Golden roast chicken with buttered peas.How to make it1.8kg whole chicken40g butter, softened1 lemon, halved4 thyme sprigs800g small potatoes, halved2 tbsp olive oil500ml milk1 brown onion, studded with 4 cloves100g fresh white breadcrumbs2 cups frozen peasRub the chicken with butter and salt, stuff with lemon and thyme, and roast at 200°C with the oiled potatoes around it.Warm the milk with the clove-studded onion and leave to infuse.Lift out the onion, stir in the breadcrumbs and a knob of butter and cook until thick.Rest the chicken, boil the peas and serve everything with the bread sauce.Sweaty-toothed madman shepherd's pieTodd's sweaty-toothed madman poem. Lamb mince under a cheddar mash crust.How to make it750g lamb mince1 tbsp olive oil1 brown onion, diced2 carrots, diced2 tbsp tomato paste2 tbsp plain flour400ml beef stock1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce1kg floury potatoes, peeled60g butter100ml milk80g cheddar, gratedBrown the mince in the oil, add the onion and carrot and cook until soft.Stir in the tomato paste and flour, then the stock and Worcestershire, and simmer until thick.Boil and mash the potatoes with the butter and milk.Spoon the filling into a dish, spread over the mash, scatter with cheddar and bake at 200°C until golden.PuddingO Captain apple pie with Vermont cheddarO Captain my Captain. Spiced apple pie with a wedge of sharp cheddar.How to make it2 sheets of frozen shortcrust pastry, thawed6 Granny Smith apples, peeled and sliced100g brown sugar2 tbsp plain flour1 tsp ground cinnamon1/4 tsp ground nutmeg1 lemon, juiced30g butter, diced1 egg, beaten150g sharp cheddar, in wedgesLine a 23cm pie dish with one sheet of pastry.Toss the apples with the sugar, flour, spices and lemon juice and pile them in, dotted with butter.Cover with the second sheet, crimp, cut steam holes and brush with egg.Bake at 190°C until golden and bubbling, then cool a little.Serve warm with a wedge of cheddar.DrinksDead Poets cave hot chocolateNeil restarts the Dead Poets Society. Thick cocoa poured from a thermos.How to make it1 L milk150g dark chocolate, chopped2 tbsp cocoa powder2 tbsp brown sugar1 tsp vanilla extractWhisk the cocoa and sugar into a little of the milk to a paste.Heat the rest of the milk, whisk in the paste and chocolate and stir until smooth and steaming.Add the vanilla and pour into a hot thermos or mugs.A cold glass of Vermont milkDing!
